text:
IT STARTED AS A QUESTION ABOUT THE CURSOR AND ENDED BY DELETING IT. AKIEN, opening: 'the workflow is inscribed on the ticket at creation time. it's order is not kept if it has to be sent back. we don't have to track the cursor that way at all. that was just the first thing that popped into my head. so what if just as only one thing can create validations, we do the same with the gates. the gate issues a license to pass, whatever that might be called.' The word already existed in the tree: CLEARANCE, harbor_master's authority rung.

WHY IT IS NOT A NEW MECHANISM. cairn/tester/validation_store.py already does exactly this for proofs: persist_validation is the single write-door, the trail is append-only, a door-minted chain digest makes a write-around detectable, and standing() DERIVES the answer with four outcomes — never sealed / newest is red / green but the source fingerprint moved / green and current. That fourth one is the interesting one, because source_fingerprint hashes the whole component and deliberately NOT git: 'a seal must expire the moment the working tree diverges, not when someone commits.' So a clearance inherits an expiry for free, and most of green-is-earned-not-assumed falls out of machinery that is already proven rather than being built again.

HIS MOTIVATION IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AND IT IS NOT THE ONE I WOULD HAVE REACHED FOR. A linear path with a cursor CANNOT REPRESENT A VOYAGE THAT WENT BACK — you either lose the order or grow the string to hold it. A dated sequence of grants and refusals loses nothing: BUILDME granted at t1, PROVEME refused at t2, BUILDME granted at t3, PROVEME granted at t4. Back-edges stop being a special case in the grammar and become more facts.

THE SAME CUT WE MADE ON SIMILARITY EDGES, ONE LAYER UP. A weight was worth storing because it is NOT recomputable from the vectors — it records what actually resolved. The derived edge was not, because it was. Here: A CLEARANCE IS A FIRST RECORD (this gate acted, at this time, on this evidence; nothing recomputes that) and THE CURSOR IS A SECOND RECORD (derivable from the clearances). By our own argument from two days earlier, the cursor is exactly the thing to delete. Two design sessions, one principle, arrived at independently — which is the strongest evidence either of them was right.

THE ADDRESS: DERIVED, NOT STORED. Akien's next move was 'then the ticket only carries the link to the file for the gate passage ticket thing.' The sharper version is that the ticket carries NOTHING NEW: validations_path_for computes where a proof's trail lives and the proof does not point at it, so a stored link would be a record of a relationship already implied — and a link can point somewhere wrong where a derived address cannot. BUT DERIVE FROM THE ID, NOT THE PATH, and this has already cost two days once: the validation door derived its address from a PROOF FILE PATH, and I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass sat unsigned for two days not awaiting a signature but awaiting an ADDRESS. Tickets migrate — at sea in CairnCommons/tickets/, then frozen into history beside the code — so the path moves and the id does not. Shape: tickets/<id>.clearances.json beside tickets/<id>.json, migrating together, mirroring validations/<stem>.json beside proofs/<stem>.py. SEPARATE FILE, because one file with two writers (the author for design fields, the gate for clearances) is the append-door trouble rebuilt on purpose.

CC'S CORRECTION, TAKEN: I said a concept-piece has no proof. AKIEN: 'of course a concept piece can have a proof, it's simply one provided by me.' The record says the door derived from a proof FILE PATH — the artifact had a proof, it had no address, and the door confused the two.

AND THE ORDER QUESTION, RULED: 'Does the class definition still declare an order, or a prerequisite graph? graph definitely.' Which retires state-machine-physics's back-edge-by-severity question outright — there is no 'how far back does a red throw you', only 'which prerequisite stopped being satisfied'.

=== THE MESH, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT MAKES A CLEARANCE WORTH ANYTHING ===

AKIEN, verbatim: 'it's not ever proof of file path for our inspections teams: it's AT LEAST proof of a not empty file. if it's supposed to be json, then it's proof of a valid json file. if it's huge, it can be the top x % sure looks like valid json. if it's json and needs to have a specific field, then we're looking for that, file is not enough. if that field has to have a range, then that's what the filter looks for.'

If gates issue clearances then A CLEARANCE IS WORTH EXACTLY WHAT ITS GATE ACTUALLY CHECKED, so the strength of the check is not an implementation detail — it is the value of the certificate. THE RULE: the check must be as strong as the claim it certifies, and existence is never the check. The ladder is a MESH GRADING, coarse to fine. This is Law 8 turned from a one-time entry condition into a standing property: a hollow build cannot pass, AND a hollow check cannot certify.

CC'S ONE ADDITION, THE FAILURE MODE IN THE SAMPLING CASE: a sampled check must RECORD ITS SAMPLE. 'Valid JSON at 5%' and 'valid JSON' are different claims, and if the clearance records only PASSED, the weaker one reads as the stronger forever after (Law 3 and Law 7 in one).

=== THE DISTINCTION THAT SAVED A MERGE ===

CC READ TWO DOCSTRINGS AND CONCLUDED THE INSPECTORS WERE TWO SPECIES — diagnostic_inspector's filters SELECT records from a log, build_inspector's filters ASSERT and red — and recommended renaming only one. AKIEN: 'oh dear no. the diagnostic inspector and the build inspector are the same mechanism with different data.' He is right and the code says so: both apply predicates to a set of measured rows, both produce FINDINGS, both are inference-free, and the 'red' is only that a non-empty selection exits 1. CC was pattern-matching on prose written at different times.

THEN THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS, FROM HIS EXPERIENCE: 'the diagnostic inspector MUST be a distinct piece of code, but built on the same principles. Why? because all other inspectors can have normal debug logging. but logging for the logging system itself... could create circular errors. so logging for the logging system itself has to work even if logging itself is broken. but the mechanisms and ideas should be roughly the same.'

THE RULE, STATED SO IT SURVIVES CONTACT: AN INSPECTOR MAY NOT BE BUILT ON WHAT IT INSPECTS. The observer of a layer cannot ride that layer, or a broken layer takes its own alarm down with it. THE SYSTEM ALREADY ARGUES THIS TWICE FROM OTHER DIRECTIONS AND NAMED IT NEITHER TIME: logger-for-bash ('booting is precisely the moment when nothing else is up yet to observe you') and transitions.py summoning build_inspector LAZILY to stay out of boot order. Three sites, one rule, re-derived each time until tonight.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: THIS DUPLICATION NEEDS A GUARD, because the danger is not drift, it is TIDINESS. The duplication looks exactly like a Law 1 defect and CC tried to merge it from reading the code — believing it was REMOVING a defect while removing the independence, and the failure would not surface until the one day it matters. Prose will not hold it (Law 4). The guard is an IMPORT-SCAN, and CLAUDE.md already owes that instrument a ticket, so this is a second customer for one build. orient's filed edge (e) was ALSO corrected: it proposes scans-and-filters as one shared library, which is right for orient and build_inspector and must never reach diagnostic_inspector — left as written it reads as a licence to merge all three.

=== AND THE NAMING, WHICH THE ABOVE SETTLED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM CC'S RECOMMENDATION ===

AKIEN: 'something went by today that made me wonder about changing the term filter to make easier for you to remember: seive. you tell me. i don't have to change it, but it's slightly more descriptive.' CC scoped the rename to build_inspector on the two-species reading, which was wrong. They are one model with a FORKED implementation — WHICH MAKES THE SHARED WORD MORE LOAD-BEARING, NOT LESS: when the code must diverge, THE VOCABULARY IS THE ONLY THING LEFT HOLDING THEM AS ONE IDEA. Renaming one and not the other would have split the model at exactly the seam where the model does all the work.

SO: one word, every inspector. SIEVE, because it is the only version where the family gains MESH — 'which mesh does this one run' is a question with an answer where 'filter strength' is not, and the ladder above IS a mesh grading. Akien's reason is the design's own: 'someone, artificial intelligence or animal intelligence or even akien intelligence all have their lives made simpler by carrying the same model.'

FOOTPRINT, MEASURED: 223 occurrences over 40 files, most of it generic Python filtering that stays 'filter'; the concept-sense concentrates in build_inspector, its proofs and its charter. TIMING IS PART OF THE RULING: before or after nothing-rides-loose adds working_tree_clean, NEVER DURING. It also overturns Akien's own verbatim wording from the 2026-07-27 ruling that founded build_inspector — permitted by Law 9 and raised by him, but the record says so rather than quietly restating him.

=== WAVE 0, RUN THE SAME NIGHT, AND IT FOUND MORE THAN IT WAS SENT FOR ===

(1) ruling-door-supersede-path IS BUILT AND ITS CURSOR IS STALE. supersede at cairn/ruling/ruling.py:303, _cmd_supersede at cli.py:98, four proofs, and the store reports 2 retired rulings so it has run in anger. Its own falsifier already said SATISFIED LIVE 2026-08-02 and was believed by nobody, because the cursor said TICKETME. An artifact whose own text contradicts its cursor is invisible to every census that reads the cursor — which is the same failure as the workflow-cursor trouble, arriving from the other side.

(2) THE DISSOLVED-STATE PROBLEM IS EXACTLY ONE BOAT. All 82 open tickets parse through parse_workflow with zero failures and none carries a dead token in its path. Of 27 berthed components, ONE rests in a dissolved state: build_inspector (to=LEARNME, standing=LEARNME). Eight others mention a dead token in prose while standing at PROVED or BUILDME — history, harmless. So it is a one-boat problem, and under the clearance ruling it may need no fix at all: no boat is IN a state, so a LEARNME clearance is just a historical fact that gates nothing.

(3) THE FINDING NOBODY WENT LOOKING FOR, AND IT IS THE EMPIRICAL CASE FOR THE WHOLE EVENING: state.json cursors carry SIXTEEN DISTINCT SHAPES across 27 components. Only 'at', 'seq' and 'standing' are universal; the rest vary — gate / from+to / build_gate / exit_gate / emission_gate / entry_gate / meter_reading / ratified_by / how_measured / closes / correcting. state.json is chartered as COMPILED FROM HISTORY AND NEVER HAND-EDITED. Sixteen shapes says it is hand-written. That is the ticket-state defect one layer over, and it is what a record with no single writer always looks like. A CLEARANCE ISSUED ONLY BY ITS GATE HAS ONE SHAPE BY CONSTRUCTION, BECAUSE ONE WRITER MEANS ONE SCHEMA. The measurement earns the ruling rather than the ruling being a preference (Law 3).

=== HOW SMALL THE BUILD ACTUALLY IS ===

history.json entries ALREADY carry a per-entry 'gate' field and are ALREADY append-only. That is a clearance with the owner missing. So the work is: delete the ticket's state string, put an OWNER on the append door, derive the trail address from the ticket id, and let state.json compile from what gates wrote. Everything else is on disk today.

=== WHAT WAS NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ===

The four rulings were opened through cairn/ruling — never hand-written into decisions/ — and every one stands UNCONFIRMED, because confirm is Akien's act and his 'agreed on all counts' is evidence for it, not a substitute. No cursor was moved: retiring sorted-renders-the-cursor and closing ruling-door-supersede-path are CROSSINGS, and crossings are not CC's to make. The sieve rename was NOT applied, because its own ruling forbids landing it during nothing-rides-loose and that ticket is live. Each ruling's what_conforms is a to-do list that reds until the work lands — which is what 'lined up' looks like in this system.
